Explanation:
Cetrimide is chemically acetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide which is classified under the group
of surface acting agents of disinfectants. (Options A, B and D are ruled out)
• Surface-active agents are substances that act on the phosphate group of cell membranes
by reducing the surface tension . After entering the cell, protein denaturation occurs.
• They act on bacteria, but have no action on spores , tubercle bacilli and most viruses .
• They are widely used as wetting agents, detergents and emulsifiers.
• The common compounds are acetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide (Cetavlon or Cetrimide )
and benzalkonium chloride .
• These are most active at alkaline pH and acid inactivates them.
• Organic matter reduces their action and anionic surface-active agents, like ordinary soaps,
render them inactive.
